# Sockguard

> A default-deny Docker socket proxy built in Go. Filter Docker API requests by method, path, and body — then layer on signed policy bundles, per-profile rollout modes, rate limits, hot-reload, and Prometheus metrics.

Sockguard sits between your Docker daemon socket and any process that needs Docker API access. Every request is filtered by method, path, and request body before it reaches the daemon. You get per-client policies (CIDR, labels, certificate selectors), signed policy bundles (cosign keyed + keyless with Rekor), container image trust verification, rollout modes (enforce/warn/audit), and Prometheus metrics.

## Key capabilities

- Default-deny: requests are blocked unless explicitly permitted by a YAML policy rule
- Method + path filtering: allow or block specific HTTP methods and URL path patterns
- Request body inspection: filter container create, exec, image pull/load, Docker and native Podman builds (including Podman additional contexts, host/local/multipart controls, and resource-usage host-file output), volume, network, secret, config, service, swarm, node, and plugin requests; bounded body reads have a 30-second deadline through logging and metrics
- Per-client policies: different rule sets per CIDR range, Docker label, TLS certificate selector (including SPKI pinning), or Unix peer credential; the trusted principal and selected profile isolate mediated BuildKit session state, with bounded persistent IDs and expiring upload grants
- Read-side redaction: strip sensitive fields from responses, keep keyword-named resources covered, and coalesce combined label plus name/image checks into one bounded inspect
- Signed policy bundles: pin keyed or keyless trust, Rekor posture, and verification timeout in a separate bootstrap file selected with --policy-bundle-trust-config; the candidate's policy_bundle block carries its signature path while bootstrap values override candidate trust fields
- Container image trust: block container or swarm-service deployment when an image isn't signed or doesn't match a trusted digest (enforce or warn mode)
- Rollout modes: enforce (deny), warn (allow + log), audit (shadow policy check without blocking) — per-profile
- Rate limits: per-profile token-bucket rate limits and global priority gates
- Hot-reload: SIGHUP or fsnotify reloads config without restarting; signature and compatibility failures preserve the active policy with bounded result labels
- Prometheus metrics: request counts, deny counts, and latency histograms with finite HTTP method and unknown-route label sets
- TLS 1.3 mTLS listener: expose a remote TCP listener with mutual TLS for multi-host setups
- Audit log: structured JSON audit log with reason codes and W3C traceparent correlation
- Active upstream watchdog: detects and reports Docker daemon unavailability via /health endpoint
